scripture.zh: 和合本（新标点和合本，神版）

note: 所有给玩家看的文字都是 { en, zh }。at 是地图上的 [x, z] 坐标（x 向东，z 向南）；r 是触发半径；fx 是剧情效果名；kind: scripture 经文 / history 考据 / imagination 游戏想象 / reflection 思考；ref 写成 Gen 1:3；hint 是这个节点结束后出现的操作提示（可以分 touch 手机 / desk 电脑两种）；card 的 after 是“哪个节点完成以后这块陶片才出现”；after（节点上的）是这个节点结束后触发的效果。第 3 章依据 docs/设计方案.md 第 4 节，创 3:1–24 一节不缺；用的是伊甸的地图。；第 6 章依据 docs/设计方案.md 第 4 节“第 6–8 章概要”里的方舟，创 6:1–8:22 一节不缺。地点在原来那张图南边另加的一块地（heightmap.ts 的 FLOOD_MAP）：北边是挪亚的地（NOAH_LAND），南边是亚拉腊山（ARARAT）；位置和方舟的尺寸在 src/episodes/gen-06-spots.ts。方舟照真实的大小造（300 × 50 × 30 肘，大约 137 × 23 × 14 米），人也是真人的大小。洪水淹过整个世界：水面涨起来，方舟跟着水浮起来、漂在水上，玩家站在方舟顶上跟着漂；方舟只在浮着的时候漂，不会从还没淹过的山顶上滑过去。n7–n10 在方舟顶上（n10 靠近顶的北边，从地上贴着墙也能走到）；陶片 remembered 也在方舟顶上。创 7:21–23 不画死亡：只有经文，水面以下什么都看不清。

sub.en: The earth is filled with wickedness

text.en: Many years later, in a land far from the old places.
text.zh: 很多年以后，在离从前的地方很远的一片地上。

text.en: Now when men began to multiply on the face of the earth and daughters were born to them,
text.zh: 当人在世上多起来、又生女儿的时候，

text.en: the sons of God saw that the daughters of men were beautiful, and they took as wives whomever they chose.
text.zh: 神的儿子们看见人的女子美貌，就随意挑选，娶来为妻。

text.en: So the LORD said, “My Spirit will not contend with man forever, for he is mortal; his days shall be 120 years.”
text.zh: 耶和华说：“人既属乎血气，我的灵就不永远住在他里面；然而他的日子还可到一百二十年。”

text.en: The Nephilim were on the earth in those days—and afterward as well—when the sons of God had relations with the daughters of men. And they bore them children who became the mighty men of old, men of renown.
text.zh: 那时候有伟人在地上，后来神的儿子们和人的女子们交合生子；那就是上古英武有名的人。

text.en: Then the LORD saw that the wickedness of man was great upon the earth, and that every inclination of the thoughts of his heart was altogether evil all the time.
text.zh: 耶和华见人在地上罪恶很大，终日所思想的尽都是恶，

text.en: And the LORD regretted that He had made man on the earth, and He was grieved in His heart.
text.zh: 耶和华就后悔造人在地上，心中忧伤。

text.en: So the LORD said, “I will blot out man, whom I have created, from the face of the earth—every man and beast and crawling creature and bird of the air—for I am grieved that I have made them.”
text.zh: 耶和华说：“我要将所造的人和走兽，并昆虫，以及空中的飞鸟，都从地上除灭，因为我造他们后悔了。”

text.en: Noah, however, found favor in the eyes of the LORD.
text.zh: 惟有挪亚在耶和华眼前蒙恩。

text.en: This is the account of Noah. Noah was a righteous man, blameless in his generation; Noah walked with God.
text.zh: 挪亚的后代记在下面。挪亚是个义人，在当时的世代是个完全人。挪亚与神同行。

text.en: And Noah had three sons: Shem, Ham, and Japheth.
text.zh: 挪亚生了三个儿子，就是闪、含、雅弗。

text.en: Now the earth was corrupt in the sight of God, and full of violence.
text.zh: 世界在神面前败坏，地上满了强暴。

text.en: And God looked upon the earth and saw that it was corrupt; for all living creatures on the earth had corrupted their ways.
text.zh: 神观看世界，见是败坏了；凡有血气的人在地上都败坏了行为。

text.en: Then God said to Noah, “The end of all living creatures has come before Me, because through them the earth is full of violence. Now behold, I will destroy both them and the earth.
text.zh: 神就对挪亚说：“凡有血气的人，他的尽头已经来到我面前；因为地上满了他们的强暴，我要把他们和地一并毁灭。

text.en: Make for yourself an ark of gopher wood; make rooms in the ark and coat it with pitch inside and out.
text.zh: 你要用歌斐木造一只方舟，分一间一间地造，里外抹上松香。

text.en: And this is how you are to build it: The ark is to be 300 cubits long, 50 cubits wide, and 30 cubits high.
text.zh: 方舟的造法乃是这样：要长三百肘，宽五十肘，高三十肘。

text.en: You are to make a roof for the ark, finish its walls a cubit from the top, place a door in the side of the ark, and build lower, middle, and upper decks.
text.zh: 方舟上边要留透光处，高一肘。方舟的门要开在旁边。方舟要分上、中、下三层。

text.en: And behold, I will bring floodwaters upon the earth to destroy every creature under the heavens that has the breath of life. Everything on the earth will perish.
text.zh: 看哪，我要使洪水泛滥在地上，毁灭天下；凡地上有血肉、有气息的活物，无一不死。

text.en: But I will establish My covenant with you, and you will enter the ark—you and your sons and your wife and your sons’ wives with you.
text.zh: 我却要与你立约；你同你的妻，与儿子儿妇，都要进入方舟。

text.en: And you are to bring two of every living creature into the ark—male and female—to keep them alive with you.
text.zh: 凡有血肉的活物，每样两个，一公一母，你要带进方舟，好在你那里保全生命。

text.en: Two of every kind of bird and animal and crawling creature will come to you to be kept alive.
text.zh: 飞鸟各从其类，牲畜各从其类，地上的昆虫各从其类，每样两个，要到你那里，好保全生命。

text.en: You are also to take for yourself every kind of food that is eaten and gather it as food for yourselves and for the animals.”
text.zh: 你要拿各样食物积蓄起来，好作你和它们的食物。”

text.en: So Noah did everything precisely as God had commanded him.
text.zh: 挪亚就这样行。凡神所吩咐的，他都照样行了。

text.en: You learned a gesture: Build. Press H (or tap “Build”) to swing a hammer.
text.zh: 你学会了一个姿态：建造。按 H 键（或点“建造”按钮），抡起锤子。

touch.zh: 你学会了“建造”：点“建造”按钮

desk.zh: 你学会了“建造”：按 H 键

text.en: Then the LORD said to Noah, “Go into the ark, you and all your family, because I have found you righteous in this generation.
text.zh: 耶和华对挪亚说：“你和你的全家都要进入方舟；因为在这世代中，我见你在我面前是义人。

text.en: You are to take with you seven pairs of every kind of clean animal, a male and its mate; a pair of every kind of unclean animal, a male and its mate;
text.zh: 凡洁净的畜类，你要带七公七母；不洁净的畜类，你要带一公一母；

text.en: and seven pairs of every kind of bird of the air, male and female, to preserve their offspring on the face of all the earth.
text.zh: 空中的飞鸟也要带七公七母，可以留种，活在全地上；

text.en: For seven days from now I will send rain on the earth for forty days and forty nights, and I will wipe from the face of the earth every living thing I have made.”
text.zh: 因为再过七天，我要降雨在地上四十昼夜，把我所造的各种活物都从地上除灭。”

text.en: And Noah did all that the LORD had commanded him.
text.zh: 挪亚就遵着耶和华所吩咐的行了。

text.en: Now Noah was 600 years old when the floodwaters came upon the earth.
text.zh: 当洪水泛滥在地上的时候，挪亚整六百岁。

text.en: And Noah and his wife, with his sons and their wives, entered the ark to escape the waters of the flood.
text.zh: 挪亚就同他的妻和儿子儿妇都进入方舟，躲避洪水。

text.en: The clean and unclean animals, the birds, and everything that crawls along the ground
text.zh: 洁净的畜类和不洁净的畜类，飞鸟并地上一切的昆虫，

text.en: came to Noah to enter the ark, two by two, male and female, as God had commanded Noah.
text.zh: 都是一对一对地，有公有母，到挪亚那里进入方舟，正如神所吩咐挪亚的。

text.en: And after seven days the floodwaters came upon the earth.
text.zh: 过了那七天，洪水泛滥在地上。

hint.en: Walk up the long ramp on the north side of the ark onto its roof.
hint.zh: 沿着方舟北边的长坡，走上方舟的顶。

sub.en: The fountains of the deep burst forth

text.en: In the six hundredth year of Noah’s life, on the seventeenth day of the second month, all the fountains of the great deep burst forth, and the floodgates of the heavens were opened.
text.zh: 当挪亚六百岁，二月十七日那一天，大渊的泉源都裂开了，天上的窗户也敞开了，

text.en: And the rain fell upon the earth for forty days and forty nights.
text.zh: 四十昼夜降大雨在地上。

text.en: On that very day Noah entered the ark, along with his sons Shem, Ham, and Japheth, and his wife, and the three wives of his sons—
text.zh: 正当那日，挪亚和他三个儿子闪、含、雅弗，并挪亚的妻子和三个儿妇，都进入方舟。

text.en: they and every kind of wild animal, livestock, crawling creature, bird, and winged creature.
text.zh: 他们和百兽，各从其类，一切牲畜，各从其类，爬在地上的昆虫，各从其类，一切禽鸟，各从其类，都进入方舟。

text.en: They came to Noah to enter the ark, two by two of every creature with the breath of life.
text.zh: 凡有血肉、有气息的活物，都一对一对地到挪亚那里，进入方舟。

text.en: And they entered, the male and female of every living thing, as God had commanded Noah. Then the LORD shut him in.
text.zh: 凡有血肉进入方舟的，都是有公有母，正如神所吩咐挪亚的。耶和华就把他关在方舟里头。

text.en: For forty days the flood kept coming on the earth, and the waters rose and lifted the ark high above the earth.
text.zh: 洪水泛滥在地上四十天，水往上长，把方舟从地上漂起。

text.en: So the waters continued to surge and rise greatly on the earth, and the ark floated on the surface of the waters.
text.zh: 水势浩大，在地上大大地往上长，方舟在水面上漂来漂去。

text.en: Finally, the waters completely prevailed upon the earth, so that all the high mountains under all the heavens were covered.
text.zh: 水势在地上极其浩大，天下的高山都淹没了。

text.en: The waters rose and covered the mountaintops to a depth of fifteen cubits.
text.zh: 水势比山高过十五肘，山岭都淹没了。

text.en: And every living thing that moved upon the earth perished—birds, livestock, animals, every creature that swarms upon the earth, and all mankind.
text.zh: 凡在地上有血肉的动物，就是飞鸟、牲畜、走兽，和爬在地上的昆虫，以及所有的人，都死了。

text.en: Of all that was on dry land, everything that had the breath of life in its nostrils died.
text.zh: 凡在旱地上、鼻孔有气息的生灵都死了。

text.en: And every living thing on the face of the earth was destroyed—man and livestock, crawling creatures and birds of the air; they were blotted out from the earth, and only Noah and those with him in the ark remained.
text.zh: 凡地上各类的活物，连人带牲畜、昆虫，以及空中的飞鸟，都从地上除灭了，只留下挪亚和那些与他同在方舟里的。

text.en: And the waters prevailed upon the earth for 150 days.
text.zh: 水势浩大，在地上共一百五十天。

text.en: But God remembered Noah and all the animals and livestock that were with him in the ark. And God sent a wind over the earth, and the waters began to subside.
text.zh: 神记念挪亚和挪亚方舟里的一切走兽牲畜。神叫风吹地，水势渐落。

text.en: The springs of the deep and the floodgates of the heavens were closed, and the rain from the sky was restrained.
text.zh: 渊源和天上的窗户都闭塞了，天上的大雨也止住了。

text.en: The waters receded steadily from the earth, and after 150 days the waters had gone down.
text.zh: 水从地上渐退。过了一百五十天，水就渐消。

text.en: On the seventeenth day of the seventh month, the ark came to rest on the mountains of Ararat.
text.zh: 七月十七日，方舟停在亚拉腊山上。

text.en: And the waters continued to recede until the tenth month, and on the first day of the tenth month the tops of the mountains became visible.
text.zh: 水又渐消，到十月初一日，山顶都现出来了。

sub.en: A raven, a dove, an olive leaf

text.en: After forty days Noah opened the window he had made in the ark
text.zh: 过了四十天，挪亚开了方舟的窗户，

text.en: and sent out a raven. It kept flying back and forth until the waters had dried up from the earth.
text.zh: 放出一只乌鸦去；那乌鸦飞来飞去，直到地上的水都干了。

text.en: Then Noah sent out a dove to see if the waters had receded from the surface of the ground.
text.zh: 他又放出一只鸽子去，要看看水从地上退了没有。

text.en: But the dove found no place to rest her foot, and she returned to him in the ark, because the waters were still covering the surface of all the earth. So he reached out his hand and brought her back inside the ark.
text.zh: 但遍地上都是水，鸽子找不着落脚之地，就回到方舟挪亚那里，挪亚伸手把鸽子接进方舟来。

text.en: Noah waited seven more days and again sent out the dove from the ark.
text.zh: 他又等了七天，再把鸽子从方舟放出去。

text.en: And behold, the dove returned to him in the evening with a freshly plucked olive leaf in her beak. So Noah knew that the waters had receded from the earth.
text.zh: 到了晚上，鸽子回到他那里，嘴里叼着一个新拧下来的橄榄叶子，挪亚就知道地上的水退了。

text.en: And Noah waited seven more days and sent out the dove again, but this time she did not return to him.
text.zh: 他又等了七天，放出鸽子去，鸽子就不再回来了。

touch.en: Jump down from the roof of the ark onto the mountain. Hold the button at the bottom right to glide down.
touch.zh: 从方舟顶上跳下去，到山顶上。按住右下角的按钮，可以慢慢滑下去

desk.en: Jump down from the roof of the ark onto the mountain. Hold Space to glide down.
desk.zh: 从方舟顶上跳下去，到山顶上。按住空格，可以慢慢滑下去

text.en: In Noah’s six hundred and first year, on the first day of the first month, the waters had dried up from the earth. So Noah removed the covering from the ark and saw that the surface of the ground was dry.
text.zh: 到挪亚六百零一岁，正月初一日，地上的水都干了。挪亚撤去方舟的盖观看，便见地面上干了。

text.en: By the twenty-seventh day of the second month, the earth was fully dry.
text.zh: 到了二月二十七日，地就都干了。

text.en: Then God said to Noah,
text.zh: 神对挪亚说：

text.en: “Come out of the ark, you and your wife, along with your sons and their wives.
text.zh: “你和你的妻子、儿子、儿妇都可以出方舟。

text.en: Bring out all the living creatures that are with you—birds, livestock, and everything that crawls upon the ground—so that they can spread out over the earth and be fruitful and multiply upon it.”
text.zh: 在你那里凡有血肉的活物，就是飞鸟、牲畜，和一切爬在地上的昆虫，都要带出来，叫它在地上多多滋生，大大兴旺。”

text.en: So Noah came out, along with his sons and his wife and his sons’ wives.
text.zh: 于是挪亚和他的妻子、儿子、儿妇都出来了。

text.en: Every living creature, every creeping thing, and every bird—everything that moves upon the earth—came out of the ark, kind by kind.
text.zh: 一切走兽、昆虫、飞鸟，和地上所有的动物，各从其类，也都出了方舟。

text.en: Then Noah built an altar to the LORD. And taking from every kind of clean animal and clean bird, he offered burnt offerings on the altar.
text.zh: 挪亚为耶和华筑了一座坛，拿各类洁净的牲畜、飞鸟献在坛上为燔祭。

text.en: When the LORD smelled the pleasing aroma, He said in His heart, “Never again will I curse the ground because of man, even though every inclination of his heart is evil from his youth. And never again will I destroy all living creatures as I have done.
text.zh: 耶和华闻那馨香之气，就心里说：“我不再因人的缘故咒诅地（人从小时心里怀着恶念），也不再按着我才行的灭各种的活物了。

text.en: As long as the earth endures, seedtime and harvest, cold and heat, summer and winter, day and night shall never cease.”
text.zh: 地还存留的时候，稼穑、寒暑、冬夏、昼夜就永不停息了。”

text.en: Day and night, summer and winter: every sunrise remembers this promise.
text.zh: 昼夜、冬夏：每一次日出，都在提醒这个应许。

text.en: “300 cubits long, 50 cubits wide, and 30 cubits high” (Genesis 6:15). A cubit is the length from the elbow to the tip of the middle finger, about 45 cm. So the ark was about 137 m long, 23 m wide and 14 m high: longer than a football field. Its length was six times its width. The ark in this game is built at this real size, and the people beside it are life-size too. Walk all the way along it and see!
text.zh: “要长三百肘，宽五十肘，高三十肘”（创 6:15）。一肘是从手肘到中指尖的长度，大约 45 厘米。算下来方舟大约长 137 米、宽 23 米、高 14 米，比一个足球场还长；长是宽的六倍。游戏里的方舟就是照这个真实的大小造的，旁边的人也是真人的大小。沿着它走一趟看看吧！

text.en: “But God remembered Noah” (Genesis 8:1). In the Bible, “remember” does not mean that God had forgotten. It means God turns toward his people and acts to help them. When have you felt that God remembered you?
text.zh: “神记念挪亚”（创 8:1）。圣经里说神“记念”，不是说神先前忘了，而是说神转向他的人，动手帮助他们。你什么时候觉得神记念了你？

title.en: The dove and the olive leaf

text.en: The dove came back with “a freshly plucked olive leaf” (Genesis 8:11), a sign that plants were growing again. Today, all over the world, a dove carrying an olive branch is a picture of peace.
text.zh: 鸽子叼回来“一个新拧下来的橄榄叶子”（创 8:11），说明地上的草木又长起来了。今天在世界各地，叼着橄榄枝的鸽子是和平的记号。

text.en: God promised that “day and night shall never cease” (Genesis 8:22). Every morning the sun rises, and every year the seasons come round again. Next time you see a sunrise, remember the promise God made after the flood.
text.zh: “昼夜就永不停息了”（创 8:22）。每天早上太阳升起，每年四季轮转。下次看见日出的时候，想一想神在洪水以后的应许。

desc.en: The dove returned in the evening with “a freshly plucked olive leaf” in her beak (Genesis 8:11). So Noah knew the waters were going down and the earth was coming back to life.
desc.zh: 到了晚上，鸽子回来，嘴里“叼着一个新拧下来的橄榄叶子”（创 8:11）。挪亚就知道水退了，地上又有了生机。

desc.en: Swing a hammer, like Noah building the ark. Learned from: Genesis 6:22.
desc.zh: 抡起锤子，像挪亚造方舟。学自：创 6:22。
